title: ConstantModulePushforwardLimit
statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category in universe u, D:I -> Scheme a diagram with affine transition maps, p_i:D_i -> X compatible qcqs structure maps, and pi:Y -> D a limit cone with qcqs structure map nu:Y -> X satisfying pi_i followed by p_i = nu. For any commutative ring Lambda and module M in universe u+1, reverse I to form the diagram of p_i,* M_Di with the canonical maps of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-pushforward-functoriality]. Its cocone into nu_* M_Y given by the projections and those same canonical maps is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 09Z1, degree-zero transition maps and continuity; Tag 09Z6, finite approximation paragraph, lines 12999-13008

proof.text: Apply Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.exists_directed (Stacks Tag 0032) to I^op to obtain a small nonempty directed partial order A and a final functor A -> I^op. Its opposite is initial. Restrict the scheme cone along this opposite functor: initiality preserves and reflects its limit property. The affine-transition and qcqs hypotheses persist. Finality preserves and reflects the colimit property of the direct-image cocone, so it suffices to prove the directed-index version.

source.place: Tag 09Z1, degree-zero transition maps and continuity; Tag 09Z6, finite approximation paragraph, lines 12999-13008

proof.text: Use the canonical constant-sheaf comparisons to identify the pullbacks of all stage constant M-sheaves to Y with M_Y. Their transitions are identities: on constant sections every pullback preserves m, and the adjunction comparisons are coherent. The colimit of this connected constant diagram is M_Y.

source.place: Tag 09Z1, degree-zero transition maps and continuity; Tag 09Z6, finite approximation paragraph, lines 12999-13008

proof.text: Apply Tag 09Z1 in degree zero to the underlying abelian sheaves. The structure maps and transitions satisfy its qcqs and affineness hypotheses. Identify R^0 p_* with p_* by left exactness. Its canonical comparison components are precisely the unit followed by the constant pullback comparison and the direct-image composition comparison, hence those of constantModulePushforwardCocone. The comparison is an isomorphism, so the underlying abelian cocone is a colimit.

source.place: Tag 09Z1, degree-zero transition maps and continuity; Tag 09Z6, finite approximation paragraph, lines 12999-13008

proof.text: Filtered colimits of module sheaves are computed by sheafifying sectionwise filtered module colimits. The underlying groups give the filtered group colimits, and sheafification is compatible with forgetting coefficients. Each displayed component is linear. Therefore the abelian colimit comparison is a linear isomorphism, and the same cocone has the module-sheaf colimit universal property. Transfer the colimit back using finality of the opposite reindexing.
